title: Quantization perf suite: GPU SKU matrix + sequence-length bins + standardized review report
author: Marcus Reed
description:
Context: Quantization Profile Library reviews need a consistent, comparable perf report across GPU SKUs and sequence-length regimes. Today our perf runner is effectively single-SKU (whatever the worker has) and aggregates results as ad-hoc console logs, which makes profile review noisy and prone to missing long-context regressions.

This PR expands the quantization perf suite to: (1) run a defined GPU SKU matrix (per-lab availability) with explicit architecture tagging, (2) bucket workloads by sequence-length bins (prefill + decode), and (3) emit a standardized report artifact (JSONL + summary markdown) that can be attached to a profile publish/review.

Key changes: Added `matrix.yaml` for GPU targets (A100-80GB sm80, H100-80GB sm90, L4 sm89, A10G sm86) and a resolver that maps worker inventory -> runnable subset. Added length bins `[0-512]`, `[513-2048]`, `[2049-8192]`, `[8193-16384]` with per-bin load-shapes (concurrency/qps) tuned to avoid OOM on smaller SKUs while still exercising batching. Implemented report writer `QuantPerfReportV1` which outputs per-run rows plus an aggregated section (p50/p95 TTFT, p50/p95 TPOT, tokens/sec, cost proxy, and deltas vs baseline).

Report artifact: `artifacts/quant_perf_report_v1.jsonl` (one JSON row per (model, variant, gpu, bin, load-shape)) + `artifacts/quant_perf_summary.md` (human-readable table sorted by speedup + any regressions).

Notes: This does not add gating/threshold enforcement in benchmark-lab itself; it only standardizes measurement + output. Gating will live in the profile publish workflow (eval/perf review).

Example summary row (markdown): `llama-3.1-8b | int8 (awq) | H100-80GB | 2k-8k | p50 TTFT 190ms (-22%) | p95 TTFT 410ms (-18%) | decode 285 tok/s (+31%)`.

Follow-ups: Add MI300X once available in the lab; wire artifact upload + permalink comment into the profile publish PR bot; expand bins for 32k+ once long-context runner stabilizes on H100.

Testing: `./bench run --suite quant-perf --dry-run` (validates matrix resolution + schema), `./bench run --suite quant-perf --gpu A100-80GB` (single-target), CI job `quant-perf-report-schema` validates JSONL rows against `schema/quant_perf_report_v1.schema.json`.
commits: bench/quant: introduce gpu matrix config + inventory resolver
bench/quant: add sequence length bins + per-bin load shapes
reporting: implement QuantPerfReportV1 JSONL writer + summary renderer
ci: add schema validation check for perf report artifacts
docs: update quant perf suite README with usage + examples
conversation:
Claire Dubois (review): Can we ensure the GPU name/arch is captured from the worker rather than trusting the matrix label? We've been bitten by mixed A100 40GB/80GB nodes.

Marcus Reed (author): Good call. Added `gpu_inventory.py` that reads `nvidia-smi -q` memory total + compute capability; report now includes `gpu_name`, `gpu_mem_gb`, and `sm` fields. Matrix entries are now match-rules rather than hard labels.

Jonas Weber (review): The bins look right, but can we split prefill vs decode lengths? Our regressions tend to be prefill-heavy in long context.

Marcus Reed (author): Added `prompt_tokens_bin` and `max_output_tokens_bin` columns per row; bins apply to prompt tokens, and output tokens are fixed per scenario (short/medium) to keep decode comparable. Summary now shows TTFT (prefill proxy) separately from TPOT.

Hiro Tanaka (review): Please include kernel compatibility info if available (flash-attn v2 vs v3, paged kv cache on/off). Otherwise perf deltas are hard to interpret across SKUs.

Marcus Reed (author): Included `runtime_features` as a stringified tag list in each row (e.g., `flashattn=v3,paged_kv=on,quant_kernel=awq_gemm_v2`). This is pulled from the runner config + runtime metadata hook.

Mateo Alvarez (review): Any guardrails to prevent OOM on L4 when running 8k bins?

Marcus Reed (author): The runner now downshifts concurrency for small-memory SKUs by bin, and enforces a max `kv_cache_bytes` budget. If a scenario would exceed the budget it is marked `skipped_reason=oom_budget` and included in the report (so reviewers see coverage gaps).

Logan Wright (review): Please add a stable identifier for cost attribution later (we want to join this with telemetry tags).

Marcus Reed (author): Added `run_id` (uuid) and `scenario_id` (deterministic hash of model+variant+gpu+bin+loadshape). Schema updated accordingly.

CI note: First run failed `quant-perf-report-schema` due to `gpu_mem_gb` being emitted as int; fixed to emit as string to match schema and reran.

Approved-by: Claire Dubois, Jonas Weber, Hiro Tanaka. Merged via squash.
release_notes: Internal: benchmark-lab quantization perf suite now supports multi-GPU matrix execution with sequence-length bins and emits a standardized `QuantPerfReportV1` artifact (JSONL + markdown summary) for quantization profile review.
